label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Thursday's launch - for Inês

Inês,

My father is ill and I am with my family in the Netherlands. I'm taking the train tonight and I don't know how long I'll be away. So Thursday is yours. I'm sorry to hand it over like this, and I'm especially sorry about the state I'm leaving it in. Below is everything I know, in the order I'd do it.

First, the most important thing. I trust you completely with this. You know the paper as well as I do, and on the sensitivity results you know it better, because you ran the annex B runs yourself. I haven't forgotten Lisbon either. When the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel and nobody in the room could tell anything had gone wrong. You are better live than you think you are. I wouldn't hand this to anyone else.

THE ERROR (read this first)

I found it this afternoon. Figure 3 and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from the old run, the one where the free allocation phase-out wasn't applied. The correct figure for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion. We had EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper doesn't change, but the headline number does. My note is in this folder ("ERROR figure 3 - must fix before launch").

This was my mistake, not yours. If anyone asks, journalists, Kessler, anyone in the room, please say exactly that: the author made an error in an earlier version, it has been corrected, and the conclusion stands. You don't have to carry it or explain it away.

Where it's already fixed:
- PDF v7 on the drive (pages 3, 14 and 15). This is the version that should go out and be linked.

Where it still needs fixing:
- Deck v4, slides 6 and 9 (slide 9 is the revenue chart)
- The embargoed press release Hanna sent on Friday to our 34 Brussels contacts, which says 2.1. The embargo lifts Thursday 26 Nov at 10:00.

WHAT TO DO, IN ORDER

1. Tuesday morning: Hanna and the press release
This one can't wait. Ask Hanna to send a corrected release to the same 34 contacts as early as possible on Tuesday, so it's well ahead of the embargo. She should keep the wording short and plain: correction to the 2030 figure, EUR 1.4 billion instead of EUR 2.1 billion, conclusions unchanged, corrected report attached. If she wants a senior name to sign off, Geert knows I'm away and has said he can do it. Please also tell her you'll be the spokesperson from now on.

2. Tuesday: Tomás at Lindqvist's office (two things)
Tomás emailed today with a timing change. The MEP has a vote moved into Thursday lunchtime and has to leave at 13:30. So:
- the presentation becomes 15 minutes instead of 20
- the panel starts at 12:50
- Lindqvist wants to take at least two questions herself before she leaves, so in practice Q&A starts during the panel, before 13:30

Please reply to confirm all of that, and tell him that you'll be presenting and sitting on the panel instead of me.

Badges: he needs the final names from our side by Wednesday 12:00 at the latest, or security won't let people in. Send him your name, plus Hanna and anyone else from the institute who is coming. Take my name off.

3. Tuesday/Wednesday: fix the deck
Change slides 6 and 9 to 1.4. The chart on slide 9 has to match figure 3 in PDF v7 exactly, so please check the axis and the label as well as the number. Then trim the talk to 15 minutes. You already cut the deck to 14 slides, so this is mostly about pace. I'd go lighter on the method slides and keep the time for the LDC results and the recommendations. My speaker notes are still in there, so use them or ignore them as you like. It's your talk now.

4. Tuesday/Wednesday: short notes to the panellists
- Abena: a quick hello saying you're presenting and I'm away for family reasons. The remote link is in the calendar invite and she tested it last week, but it's worth one more test on Wednesday if she has time.
- Kessler: a short, courteous line saying you're replacing me. You don't need to mention the correction, though he will have it from the press release anyway.

5. Wednesday 14:00 and 15:00: the press calls
Hanna set up two 20-minute background calls, one with a trade newsletter and one with a Belgian daily. Please take them. Ask Hanna to confirm the times with them and to tell them it's you. Open with the corrected number yourself, before they bring it up. Then move on to what the paper actually says.

6. Thursday
Guests at the security entrance by 12:00, and Tomás collects the badges. Light lunch outside the room from 12:00. Updated run of show:
- 12:30 Lindqvist welcome (5 min)
- 12:35 your presentation (15 min)
- 12:50 panel: Abena (remote), Kessler, you. Lindqvist moderates.
- Lindqvist takes her two questions and leaves at 13:30, so check with Tomás who moderates the rest. If nobody is named, offer to do it yourself or ask Abena to help close.
- 14:00 close

Please get someone (Hanna?) to take photos and count attendance. We need those for the Halvorsen Foundation, see point 7.

KESSLER

He's going to try to make the whole panel about the 80% pass-through assumption in section 4. Don't let him set the tone. Acknowledge the point and answer it in one go, openly and without getting defensive, then bring the discussion back to the LDCs, which is what the paper is actually about.

My reply lines (also in this folder):
- 80% is the central case. Annex B runs 60% and 40%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say it as it is. This is your own work, so you'll explain it better than I would.
- Resource shuffling: we agree it's a risk, it's covered in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report.
- Abena will probably back us on the LDC side. She was strong on our call. Give her room to come in.

If he brings up the 2.1 figure, that's my mistake, it's corrected, and the conclusion is the same. Then move on.

7. After the launch: Halvorsen Foundation
Lucy Tran (programme officer) is coming with a colleague. For their grant report they need two photos from the event and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. She also congratulated both of us on finishing it, and she's right to.

WHERE THINGS ARE
All in this folder on the drive (border-revenues-launch):
- Run of show (my version from 20 Nov, now out of date on timings, see above)
- ERROR figure 3 note
- PDF v7: the corrected report
- Deck v4 plus your notes
- Kessler's comments on the draft and my reply lines

Emails I'm forwarding to you tonight: Tomás (timings and badges), Hanna (press release and journalist calls), Lucy Tran (Halvorsen).

REACHING ME
You can call me. Before 9 tomorrow morning is the best time. After that I may not pick up, and I don't know yet how it will go after that. If something needs a decision and you can't reach me, decide it yourself. I mean that. If you need a senior name, go to Geert.

I'm sorry to leave you with this, and especially with an error I should have caught weeks ago. But I'm not worried about Thursday at all. You'll do it well.

Marieke
